title: GoHighLevel vs Keap 2026: Real Pricing and Honest Verdict

body:
GoHighLevel vs Keap: the short answer

Quick verdict: Keap is a CRM you buy to run your own business. GoHighLevel is a CRM you buy to run other people's businesses. If two people will ever log in, Keap is the more comfortable product and the more expensive one. If three or more people log in, or if you serve more than one client, GoHighLevel wins on structure and never charges you for the extra seats.

The single fact that decides most of these comparisons: Keap includes 2 users and charges $39 per month for every user after that. GoHighLevel gives unlimited users on every plan, including the $97 one. Both numbers are published by the vendors themselves and both were re-verified on 12 August 2026.

The real price difference is your team size

Keap has abandoned feature-based tiers. There is now one platform at $299 per month billed monthly, or $2,988 per year, which works out to $249 per month if you commit annually. That price includes 2 user licences and a contact allowance that scales in tiers.

GoHighLevel publishes three plans: Starter $97 per month or $970 per year (3 sub-accounts), Unlimited $297 per month or $2,970 per year (unlimited sub-accounts, rebill phone and email at cost), and Agency Pro $497 per month or $4,970 per year (SaaS Mode, rebilling with your own markup).

Here is where it gets interesting. At exactly two users, Keap's annual price of $2,988 and GoHighLevel's Unlimited annual price of $2,970 are $18 apart for the year. They are effectively the same product cost. Every user you add after the second one costs $39 a month on Keap and nothing at all on GoHighLevel.

Monthly cost as the team grows, using each vendor's published rates:

  • 2 users: Keap $299, GoHighLevel Starter $97, GoHighLevel Unlimited $297.
  • 5 users: Keap $416, GoHighLevel unchanged at $97 or $297.
  • 10 users: Keap $611, GoHighLevel unchanged at $97 or $297.
  • 25 users: Keap $1,196, GoHighLevel unchanged at $97 or $297.

On annual billing a ten person team pays Keap $6,732 a year ($2,988 plus eight extra users at $39 a month) against $2,970 for GoHighLevel Unlimited. That is 2.27 times more for the same headcount, and the gap widens with every hire.

Two more contract details worth knowing before you compare the headline numbers. Keap's $249 effective rate requires a one year commitment, and cancelling inside that term carries a $299 early termination fee. GoHighLevel is month to month with no contract and you can cancel from the dashboard.

Keap's text tiers: the arithmetic buyers miss

Keap bundles text marketing Tier 1 into every subscription: 500 messages and 100 voice minutes, with overage charged at $0.015 per message and $0.01 per voice minute. You can upgrade to five paid tiers. We ran the arithmetic on Keap's own published table and the result surprised us.

Compare what each tier costs against what the same extra usage would cost as overage on Tier 1:

  • Tier 2 at $24 buys 500 extra messages and 200 extra minutes. As overage that is $9.50 of usage. You lose $14.50.
  • Tier 3 at $39 buys 2,000 messages and 400 minutes, worth $34. You lose $5.
  • Tier 4 at $79 buys 4,500 messages and 700 minutes, worth $74.50. You lose $4.50.
  • Tier 5 at $139 buys 9,500 messages and 900 minutes, worth $151.50. You finally gain $12.50.
  • Tier 6 at $279 buys 24,500 messages and 1,900 minutes, worth $386.50. You gain $107.50.

So on Keap's published numbers, tiers 2, 3 and 4 all cost more than the usage they replace. Tier 5 is the first upgrade that pays for itself. If you send fewer than about 10,000 texts a month, staying on the included tier and paying overage is cheaper than upgrading.

There is a cheaper route still. Keap lists an optional add-on of 500 texts for $6, which is $0.012 per message, twenty percent below the $0.015 overage rate. The pricing page does not state whether those blocks stack, so confirm that with Keap before planning around it, but if they do, the add-on beats every tier up to Tier 6.

None of this makes Keap a bad product. It means the sensible Keap buyer ignores the middle of the text menu, which is not something the menu tells you.

Where HighLevel gets expensive

We earn a commission if you sign up to GoHighLevel through this page, so the useful thing we can do is show you where it loses.

The subscription is not the bill. Phone numbers, SMS, email and premium AI are all usage-based on top, on every plan. And several add-ons cost as much as the plans they sit on:

  • Premium support is $500 a month. That is 1.7 times the entire Unlimited plan and 5.2 times the Starter plan. Keap includes a dedicated Customer Success Manager, US based phone support and 24/7 chat in its base price.
  • HIPAA compliance is $297 a month, exactly the price of the Unlimited plan it attaches to.
  • The white label mobile app is $497 a month, exactly the price of the entire Agency Pro plan. The desktop web app can be white labelled at no extra cost, so "white label" means two very different things here.
  • AI Employee is $50 or $97 per month per sub-account. Turn the Unlimited plan on for ten clients and that is $500 to $970 a month on top of a $297 subscription, up to 3.3 times the plan itself.
  • Other published add-ons: SEO $79, branded client portal $49, online listings $30, premium prospecting $29 and WhatsApp $10, all per sub-account per month, plus dedicated email IPs at $59 per IP.

The honest framing is that GoHighLevel's cheap sticker price buys you the platform, not the outcome. Budget for usage and for at least one add-on per client.

The agency question: can you resell it?

This is the part that ends the comparison for most agencies. GoHighLevel's Agency Pro plan at $497 includes SaaS Mode, which turns the platform into your own sellable software: you set the price, client accounts are created automatically, and you rebill SMS and email usage with your own markup. The Unlimited plan at $297 lets you rebill at cost with no markup.

Keap has no equivalent. It has an affiliate and certified partner programme, but you cannot white label Keap, resell it as your own product, or manage separate client environments inside one account. Keap is architecturally a single business tool. GoHighLevel gives you 3 sub-accounts on the $97 plan and unlimited sub-accounts from $297.

If you have never wanted to resell software, this section does not matter and you should weight the rest more heavily. If you have, there is no contest.

Try GoHighLevel free for 14 days, or read our full guide to SaaS Mode before you commit to the $497 tier.

Support and setup: Keap's strongest card

Keap requires an implementation package with every subscription. It covers a business mapping session, done-for-you automations, data import, migration, third party integrations and recurring strategy calls. Keap argues, reasonably, that most small businesses who buy automation software never actually implement it.

There is a real catch, and it is the biggest gap in Keap's pricing transparency: the implementation package is required and its price is not published on the pricing page. You can compute your total GoHighLevel cost from GoHighLevel's own pricing page, including all fourteen add-ons. You cannot compute Keap's without talking to sales.

GoHighLevel's answer to onboarding is a library of prebuilt account snapshots, a large user community and 24/7 support, with premium support sold separately. That works if you or someone on your team enjoys building systems. It does not replace a consultant, and agencies routinely hire help to get set up, which is a real cost most comparisons ignore. If that is you, hiring a GoHighLevel developer is usually cheaper than the year you spend learning it.

Choose Keap if you are one business

  • You run a single business, not an agency, and one or two people use the CRM.
  • You want a human being assigned to your account and hands-on implementation included.
  • You would rather have one plan with everything than pick a tier.
  • You send modest text volume and value 500 messages being bundled in.
  • You want a native payment processor, quotes, invoices, order bumps and promo codes without assembly.

Choose GoHighLevel if you have a team

  • Three or more people will log in, where Keap's per-user fee starts compounding.
  • You serve multiple clients and need separate sub-accounts.
  • You want the option to resell the platform under your own brand.
  • You want to know your full cost before you speak to a salesperson.
  • You want month to month billing with no early termination fee.

The verdict

Keap is the better experience for a small team that wants to be looked after, and it is priced accordingly. GoHighLevel is the better economics for anyone with a team or clients, and it is the only one of the two you can turn into a product you sell.

The cleanest way to decide: count the people who will log in. At two, the two platforms cost within $18 a year of each other and you should pick on support and setup, where Keap is genuinely stronger. Past two, Keap's price climbs by $468 per person per year and GoHighLevel's does not move, and no amount of onboarding closes that gap.

Can you resell Keap the way you can resell GoHighLevel?

No. GoHighLevel's Agency Pro plan at $497 per month includes SaaS Mode, which lets you sell the platform as your own branded software, create client accounts automatically and rebill SMS and email with your own markup. Keap has an affiliate and certified partner programme but cannot be white labelled or resold as your own product, and it has no sub-account architecture for managing separate clients.
How much does Keap really cost once implementation is added?

Keap does not publish that number. Its pricing page states that an implementation package is required with every subscription, covering business mapping, done-for-you automations, data import, migration and strategy calls, but the price is only available through sales. This is the main transparency gap between the two: you can calculate a full GoHighLevel bill from its pricing page, including all of its add-ons, and you cannot do the same for Keap.
Which is better for a solo business owner?

Keap, in most cases. At one or two users the subscription costs are close, and Keap includes a dedicated Customer Success Manager, US based phone support, 24/7 chat and hands-on implementation, where GoHighLevel sells premium support separately at $500 per month. Keap also bundles 500 text messages and 100 voice minutes. GoHighLevel still wins on raw price at $97, but a solo owner who does not enjoy building systems will get more value from Keap.
